issues.legal_issue: A fresh suit on the same cause of action may be presented after rejection of an earlier plaint, but remains subject to the applicable limitation period.

A second suit for specific performance filed after rejection of an earlier plaint is governed by the residuary three-year limitation period under Article 113 of the Limitation Act, rather than Article 54.
The right to file a fresh suit under Order VII Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure accrues upon rejection of the earlier plaint, and the limitation period for that suit runs from that rejection.
A plaint may be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) where, on a holistic reading of its averments and the admitted facts, the suit is plainly barred by limitation, without recording evidence.
